subject: Crestline wiring and fallback validation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan@crestline.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Crestline wiring and fallback validation

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our follow-up, I wanted to kick off a short technical validation thread so we can align on integration wiring and fallback behavior before the POC. High-level asks below: 

- Quick topology sketch (ingress, VPC/VNet, any private peering) — I attached a draft topology to start (crestline-topology-v1.drawio).
- Confirmation on expected request routing (do you plan on outbound to our hosted API, or prefer we deploy a private Redwood connector in your VPC?).
- Desired fallback policy: is it acceptable to fail to a lower-capacity model or must we preserve identical output semantics?
- Test matrix: API-level smoke tests, latency SLOs under synthetic load, and KV-cache warmup scenarios.

Can we schedule a 45-min sync next week (I’m in PST) to walk the topology and agree owners? If you can share an infra snippet (k8s/ingress/egress rules) that will help us prepare.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Sergio (runtime/routing) and Marissa (test harness) on our side.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: crestline-topology-v1.drawio (drawio diagram stub)
From: Ethan Rogers <ethan@crestline.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestline wiring and fallback validation

Thanks, Priyom — and appreciate the clear list. Attached is an infra snippet and a short note from our infra lead describing constraints. High level answers up front: 

- We run on k8s in a customer-dedicated VPC; outbound egress is via NAT gateway. We’d prefer not to open inbound peering to a hosted endpoint — goal is to avoid inbound network reachability.
- For the POC we are open to using a private connector (your VPC appliance) or an authenticated outbound call to your hosted API, whichever is simpler operationally for us.
- Fallback: Our primary requirement is semantic fidelity for user-critical flows (payments/agreements). For non-critical flows (search/completions) we can tolerate lower-cost model variants. We’ll flag user-facing intents that require strict fidelity.

Questions for you: 
1) Can Redwood’s KV cache warmup be seeded from our user session store during cold-starts? We want deterministic short-tail latency on first few tokens.
2) If we use a private connector, how do we handle model variant routing (hosted -> dedicated -> private) in the event of capacity degradation? Do you support automatic fallback with optional routing policies per-route?

Attaching: crestline-infra-snippet.yaml

Available for a sync Thu/Fri PST — let me know times.

—Ethan
Ethan Rogers
Head of Engineering, Crestline
ethan@crestline.io

Attachment: crestline-infra-snippet.yaml (yaml stub)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Crestline wiring and fallback validation

Forwarding Ethan’s infra note — see inline below. Quick internal split of work and asks: 

- Sergio: can you confirm runtime-level options for outbound-only customer deployments and the exact behavior of our routing policies when model capacity becomes constrained? Key callouts: KV cache seeding from customer session store, and whether we can do rule-based routing (e.g. route critical intents to Dedicated with hard SLO).
- Marissa: can you prepare a lightweight test harness that can run in Crestline’s k8s (a Job/Pod) to exercise warm-cold KV cache scenarios and synthetic burst loads up to 500qps? We need smoke tests for correctness and perf.
- Me: I’ll coordinate the sync and capture any required compliance artifacts (NDA/terms).

Proposed internal prep: 30-min run-through Tue 9/9 10am PST — please confirm or propose alternative.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Crestline wiring and fallback validation

Priyom — quick ack and plan: 

Sergio: I’ll take point on the routing/fallback behavior. Initial notes: we support route policies that can be per-intent or per-route, and we can pin critical intents to Dedicated capacity with hard fallthrough to a labeled model variant (same architecture, lower precision) if Dedicated is unavailable. I’ll validate whether we can enforce outbound-only connector semantics without inbound peering (short answer: yes, via an outbound TLS tunnel + mutual auth connector). Will produce a short runbook with explicit traffic diagrams by EOD Monday.

Marissa: I’ll produce the harness and a k8s Job example. Plan: harness will seed the cache via a REST call to a small seeding endpoint (we’ll provide a lightweight container) and then execute randomized prompt sets to validate semantic parity and latency percentiles. I can target 500qps for short bursts; we’ll also include a long-tail test (10m sustained at 100qps). I’ll add a checklist for gating (token-level diffs, error-rate thresholds, 95th latency).

We’ll aim to have artifacts in the Crestline folder on Drive and a runbook draft before the sync.

Sergio

From: Ethan Rogers <ethan@crestline.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestline wiring and fallback validation

Sounds good — thanks all. Thu 9/10 10am PST works for us for the sync. I’ve attached a signed copy of the mutual NDA and a short list of critical intents (payments/create_agreement/update_contract) that we want pinned to strict-fidelity routing.

Two practical notes: 
- For the seeding workflow, we can accept a one-time REST call that pulls a user session snapshot from our store (we can provide a temp token-limited endpoint).
- For model fallbacks, we prefer a policy that allows pinning by intent name and an opt-in for logging diffs when fallback occurs (so we can review regressions).

See attached: crestline-nda-signed.pdf

—Ethan
